significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would license a form-(iii) conclusion: across scientific foundation models, greater geometric isomorphism to a canonical ontology, summarized by the "Relational-Fidelity Score," predicts stronger generalization to "held-out entities and relations." This establishes a weighty representational phenomenon and fixes expected model rankings and generalization outcomes, but not a causal internal mechanism; that distinction matters because probing work such as Hewitt and Liang (2019) shows that decodable structure alone need not establish how a model computes. Verified false would rule out ontology fidelity as a general proxy for structural understanding, although the bundled axes, clusters, tree metrics, and "genuine ... versus co-occurrence memorization" language make partial refutations less decisive; nevertheless, global true and false outcomes are distinguishable. Topic-substitution check: the broad topic alone would not earn this score—the specific fidelity-to-generalization predictive coupling, which is false of the median concept-probing proposal, supports the above-median rating.

reach.justification: The named handle is the "Relational-Fidelity Score combining axis-recovery R^2, cluster purity, and metric-correlation," intended as a "read-only diagnostic" rather than merely an explanatory visualization. It is ex ante because the claim says fidelity "predicts the model's downstream generalization," giving auditors a possible basis for screening or ranking models before attempting held-out entities, although it does not by itself prove that co-occurrence and understanding are cleanly separable. After ontology-specific re-extraction, the substantive prediction survives as a transferable relation—higher fidelity should imply better extrapolation—and the hypothesis asserts scope across chemistry, biology, materials, multiple model families, sizes, and ontology types, with potential uptake by model evaluators and scientific-model practitioners. Topic-substitution check: deleting the relational-fidelity predictor leaves only generic scientific-representation analysis, which would not justify this reach; the portable score and forward predictive coupling are the claim-specific reasons for the high band.
